sample.title: Stun grenades banned in French student protests after teenager's hand blown off | BBC News
sample.description:
The French government has suspended the use of stun grenades by police in school protests, as it appeals to students to go back to the classroom.
 
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez has temporarily halted the use of the grenades after a 15-year-old's hand was blown off by a grenade fired by riot police near a school in Northern France. An investigation into the event has been launched.
 
Wider allegations have been made of excessive use of force by police in dealing with the protests which began at the start of October.
 
More schools reopened on Wednesday, although some remained blockaded, after an estimated 250,000 people took to the streets demonstrating over school conditions on Tuesday.

sample.title: 7 October survivors debate how to rebuild homes | BBC News
sample.description:
As Israel marks the third anniversary of the 7 October Hamas attacks, the BBC has visited residents of kibbutz Nir Oz - one of the worst hit places.

Sitting just a mile (1.6km) from the Gaza border, 41 Nir Oz residents and foreign workers were killed along with six people who had fled to the kibbutz from a party nearby. Seventy-six people from the kibbutz were kidnapped to Gaza, including nine bodies. Fourteen of those hostages were taken alive and killed in captivity.

During the October 7 attack, about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage. The ensuing war between Israel and Hamas has killed more than 74,200 people in Gaza according to the Hamas-run health ministry – whose overall figures are seen as accurate by the UN.

sample.title: Christa Pike 'conscious and speaking' after failed execution, lawyers say | BBC News
sample.description:
US death row inmate Christa Pike is "conscious and speaking" after surviving a failed execution attempt in the state of Tennessee last week, her lawyers say.
 
Pike, 50, continues to receive critical medical care while handcuffed in hospital, according to a statement from her attorneys on Tuesday.
 
She was sentenced to death following her conviction for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995. But Pike survived two lethal injections last Wednesday and was transferred to a hospital in Nashville for treatment, where she remained unconscious while medical staff cleared her body of the injected pentobarbital.
 
An anaesthesiologist advising Pike's defence team said her survival is highly unusual.

sample.title: Russia plague fears after death of lab worker at research centre | BBC News
sample.description:
The death of a worker at a Russian plague research centre in Siberia has raised concerns that the deadly disease could spread.

The World Health Organisation and the United States have both asked Russia for more information on the circumstances surrounding the incident.   US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has urged Russia to release more information.  "I think it's incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more information with the world," Rubio told reporters. "We're watching it very closely, hour by hour."

The incident has sparked a flurry of speculation about the circumstances in which the 28-year-old woman died. Russian officials have said they are still investigating the cause of the death but those who came into contact with the victim all tested negative to pneumonic plague.

Reports first emerged on Friday of almost 200 people being placed under observation in Siberia's Irkutsk region following the death.
The lab worker, named in Russian media as Darya Shipilova, had reportedly fallen ill a couple of days earlier.

Unconfirmed reports suggested that she had become ill after breaking a test tube containing the pathogen or following a field trip to a region where plague occurs naturally among wild rodents.

But Russian officials have played down those reports. The country's health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor said the woman had died of "pneumonia of an undetermined etiology".
